script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - MORNING

A small, quaint coffee shop nestled in the heart of a quaint, picturesque small town. The sun filters through the windows, casting dappled light on the worn wooden tables and mismatched chairs.

A young woman, LUCY, sits at a table, her laptop open in front of her. She looks up as the door jingles and in walks JASPER, a man in his mid-30s. He's tall, with a shaggy beard and a kind smile.

LUCY
(cheerfully)
Morning, Jasper.

JASPER
(returning the smile)
Morning, Lucy. How's your novel coming along?

LUCY
(sighs)
Slowly. But I'll get there.

They fall into a comfortable silence as Jasper orders his coffee and Lucy continues to type.

EXT. TOWN SQUARE - DAY

Lucy and Jasper sit on a bench in the town square, surrounded by vibrant flowers and the sounds of children playing in the distance.

LUCY
You know, I've been thinking... I feel like this town is suffocating me.

JASPER
(surprised)
Really? I've always thought you seemed happy here.

LUCY
(shaking her head)
I am, but I feel like there's something more out there for me. Something I haven't discovered yet.

JASPER
Well, maybe you just need a change of pace. Have you thought about traveling?

LUCY
(nods)
I have. But I don't have the means to do it on my own.

JASPER
(smiling)
Well, I just happen to know someone who might be able to help you with that.

INT. JASPER'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Lucy sits on the couch in Jasper's cozy apartment, her laptop open in front of her. Jasper paces back and forth, deep in thought.

JASPER
(stops pacing)
I have an idea. There's a grant for writers to travel and research their novels. I can help you apply.

LUCY
(looking up, shocked)
Really? You'd do that for me?

JASPER
(smiling)
Of course. I believe in you and your writing.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - MORNING

Lucy sits at the same table, her laptop open in front of her. Jasper enters, holding a stack of papers.

JASPER
(setting the papers down)
I've got everything you need to apply for the grant. Let me know if there's anything else you need.

LUCY
(tearfully)
Thank you, Jasper. This means the world to me.

EXT. TOWN SQUARE - DAY

Lucy sits on the bench in the town square, her laptop open in front of her. She looks up as Jasper approaches, holding a camera.

JASPER
I thought we could take some pictures for your grant application. What do you think?

LUCY
(smiling)
That's a great idea.

They spend the afternoon taking pictures of the town and its people, capturing the essence of small-town life.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Lucy sits at the same table, her laptop open in front of her. Jasper enters, holding a letter.

JASPER
(holding out the letter)
Your grant application was approved.

LUCY
(tearfully)
I can't believe it. Thank you, Jasper. You made this possible.

JASPER
(smiling)
No, Lucy. You did. You have the talent and the drive. I just helped you see it.

EXT. TOWN SQUARE - MORNING

Lucy and Jasper sit on the bench in the town square, watching as the sun rises over the horizon.

LUCY
I'm going to miss this place. But I know I need to go and discover new things.

JASPER
(smiling)
I know you will. And I'll be here, waiting for your next masterpiece.

They share a warm, understanding smile as the camera pans out, leaving them sitting in the peaceful town square, a symbol of the small-town life that had shaped them, but was now ready to let them go and discover the world beyond.

THE END.
